findings.subject: radio
findings.summary: In forced-colors mode a checked radio looks the same as an unchecked one.
findings.evidence: radio.css:78-84 (dot is a ::before with background-color) and radio.css:91-94 (fill is background-color); no @media (forced-colors) rule in radio.css (grep across the batch: only button.css has one). Forced colors replace background-color with Canvas. Derived from CSS, not observed at runtime.
findings.fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) { .a63-Radio-indicator::before { background-color: CanvasText; forced-color-adjust: none } .a63-Radio[data-checked] { border-color: Highlight } } (or draw the dot with a border), and capture a forced-colors story.

verified.reason: radio.css shows the checked state only through background-color (indicator fill, ::before dot at 78-84 and 91-94) and border-color. The repo has no forced-colors rule except in button.css. Base UI Radio is a span, not a native input. Under forced colors both backgrounds become Canvas and the border becomes the system color, so checked and unchecked look the same. Not run in a browser, but the CSS reasoning holds.

findings.subject: switch
findings.summary: Under dir=rtl the checked thumb slides out of the track.
findings.evidence: switch.css:43-45 (inline-flex track), 88-89 (transform: translateX(var(--thumb-x)), transform-origin: left), 116-120 (--thumb-x: var(--switch-thumb) when checked). No :dir()/[dir=rtl] rule in the batch or packages/styles (grep). In RTL the off thumb sits at the right edge and a positive translateX pushes it a thumb-width past it. No RTL story or test.
findings.fix: Negate the travel in RTL (e.g. .a63-Switch:dir(rtl) .a63-Switch-thumb { --thumb-x-sign: -1 } and translateX(calc(var(--thumb-x) * var(--thumb-x-sign, 1))), transform-origin inline-start/end), and add an RTL story with a baseline.

verified.reason: switch.css uses an inline-flex track, so in RTL the thumb starts at the right edge. Checked adds translateX(+thumb), a physical shift to the right, with transform-origin left/right. No :dir() or [dir=rtl] rule touches the switch; the repo only has RTL rules for calendar, carousel, breadcrumb and scrollable-list. In RTL the checked thumb moves past the track's right edge.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: ui-react never provides Base UI's DirectionProvider, so in RTL the slider renders mirrored but drags and steps left-to-right.
findings.evidence: grep 'DirectionProvider' in packages/ui-react/src: no match. node_modules/@base-ui/react/direction-provider/DirectionProvider.mjs:14 defaults direction to 'ltr'; slider/control/SliderControl.mjs and slider/thumb/SliderThumb.mjs read it, while SliderThumb.mjs:194 positions with CSS insetInlineStart. The same missing provider affects arrow-key direction in RadioGroup and the SegmentedControl tabs. Not run in a browser.
findings.fix: Have UIProvider accept or detect dir and render <DirectionProvider direction={dir}>; add an RTL story for slider, radio and segmented-control and an interaction test that ArrowRight decreases in RTL.

verified.reason: Nothing in packages or docs mentions DirectionProvider. Base UI's useDirection returns 'ltr' when no provider is present (DirectionContext.mjs). SliderControl uses it for pointer math (line 169) and SliderThumb for key steps (110-114), but the thumb is placed with insetInlineStart (194), so under dir=rtl the slider renders mirrored while pointer and key math stay LTR. Composite (RadioGroup, Tabs) also reads direction. Nothing documents that consumers must add the provider themselves.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: SegmentedControl accepts no pass-through props or ref and works only controlled.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.tsx:21-35 (closed props interface: no ...rest, no ref, no aria-*/id/data-*), 28 and 33 (onValueChange and value required, no defaultValue), 56-70 (nothing spread onto Tabs.Root).
findings.fix: Type props as Omit<Tabs.Root.Props, 'onValueChange'|'value'|'defaultValue'> plus the contract axes, spread rest onto the root, add defaultValue (uncontrolled), and make value/onValueChange optional.

verified.reason: SegmentedControlProps (segmented-control.tsx:21-35) is a closed interface: no rest spread, no ref, no aria-*, id or data-*. value and onValueChange are required, with no defaultValue, and nothing is spread onto Tabs.Root. K1 requires spread props, a forwarded ref, and both controlled and uncontrolled modes.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: SegmentedControl exposes tabs with no panels and an unnameable tablist, and selection does not follow arrow keys.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.tsx:9,56-105 (Base UI Tabs, no Tabs.Panel); TabsList.d.ts:15-18 (activateOnFocus default false, not set); no way to pass aria-label to the tablist (k02-choice-4); segmented-control.json has no accessibility pattern and patterns.test.ts binds none for it. Contract promises 'Preserves single selection semantics'.
findings.fix: Rebuild on Base UI RadioGroup (or ToggleGroup with single selection) so it is a named radiogroup whose arrow keys move selection, keep the sliding indicator, bind the APG radio pattern in the contract and patterns.test.ts.

verified.reason: The code matches: Base UI Tabs with no Tabs.Panel, activateOnFocus not set, and no way to name the tablist. The severity is inflated, though. aria-selected keeps single-selection semantics (the contract outcome holds), and manual activation is allowed by the APG tabs pattern. The tablist naming gap comes from k02-choice-4. What is left is a role mismatch (tabs without panels, where radiogroup or toggle-group semantics fit better), which is a quality gap rather than an inaccessible control.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: A controlled range slider is impossible: onValueChange reports only the first thumb.
findings.evidence: slider.tsx:19-22 (Base UI onValueChange omitted), 30-34 and 81-83 (handler forwards next[0] for arrays). Contract modes include 'range' (CLI). Ranged story is uncontrolled (slider.stories.tsx:35-41); no test for controlled range.
findings.fix: Type onValueChange as (value: number | number[], details) like Base UI, or add onValuesChange(values: number[]); add a controlled Ranged story and test.

verified.reason: slider.tsx omits Base UI's onValueChange (19-22) and forwards only next[0] for arrays (81-83). A consumer passing value=[a,b] never receives the second thumb's value, so a live controlled range slider cannot work; onValueCommitted via rest props only fires on commit. The range story is uncontrolled. Confirmed from source.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: In forced-colors mode filled and empty stars look the same, so the score and the selected value disappear.
findings.evidence: rating.css:11-12 (on = amber, off = text-secondary 35%), 48-53 (glyph fill/stroke currentColor), 62 and 80-81 (state = color only); no forced-colors rule. Forced colors map every color to one system color. Empty-star contrast (35% alpha secondary text) also likely below 3:1; not measured.
findings.fix: In @media (forced-colors: active) draw off stars as outline only (fill: none; stroke: CanvasText) and on stars filled with Highlight (forced-color-adjust: none); raise --rating-off to a token that meets 3:1.

verified.reason: rating.css draws on and off stars only through color (11-12, 62, 80-81), with the SVG fill and stroke set to currentColor (48-53), and it has no forced-colors rule. Forced colors map color to a system color, so on and off stars render identically. A read-only score disappears visually, and so does the selected value. Not run in a browser, but the CSS reasoning holds.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: In forced-colors mode the progress fill disappears; with reduced motion the indeterminate bar reads as 40% done.
findings.evidence: progress.css:35-50 (fill = background-color only), no forced-colors rule; progress.css:52-55 and 73-78 (indeterminate = width 40%, animation removed under reduced motion).
findings.fix: Forced colors: .a63-Progress-indicator { background-color: Highlight; forced-color-adjust: none }. Reduced motion: give the indeterminate state a distinct static treatment (e.g. full-width striped or pulsing-opacity-free dashed fill) instead of a 40% bar.

verified.reason: The progress fill is background-color only (35-50) with no forced-colors rule, so under forced colors the fill and track both become Canvas and the progress is lost. Under reduced motion the indeterminate indicator keeps width:40% with the animation removed (52-55, 73-78), so it reads as a static 40% bar. Both confirmed from the CSS.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: The invalid state is styled and listed in the contract but no story or baseline shows it.
findings.evidence: checkbox.css:109-111; contract states include invalid (CLI); grep 'invalid' checkbox.stories.tsx: none; ui-react-checkbox-states-chromium-linux.png shows 5 boxes, none invalid.
findings.fix: Add an invalid checkbox (aria-invalid) to the States story, as radio.stories.tsx:116 does.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: The required disabled state has no story or baseline.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.json requiredStates [rest, selected, disabled]; grep 'disabled' segmented-control.stories.tsx: none; disabled only in segmented-control.test.tsx:69; css:112-115.
findings.fix: Add a story with one disabled segment (and the accent tone) so it is captured in the visual baselines.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Segments are shorter than 44px on coarse pointers.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.css:18-22 (height floors at --a63-control-min-size, 2rem on coarse per environment.css:130), 68 (only min-width uses min-target), 87-92 (::after extends by --segment-inset only). Derived target about 30px (md) / 26px (sm); not measured; check:control-alignment does not cover SegmentedControl.
findings.fix: Extend each item's ::after block-size to max(100% + 2*inset, --a63-control-min-target) like Button's ::before, and add SegmentedControl to check-control-alignment.mjs.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Long labels overflow instead of truncating, and every segment repeats its visible label as a native tooltip.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.css:64 (items flex: none) makes the ellipsis rule at css:156-160 inert outside fullWidth; segmented-control.tsx:74,79 (aria-label and title always set to item.label). Keyboard direction in RTL: k02-choice-3.
findings.fix: Allow items to shrink (min-width: 0 with a max inline size) so ellipsis applies, set title only for the icon variant or truncated labels, and drop aria-label when the label is visible.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Keyboard behaviour and accessibility semantics are untested.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.test.tsx:15-69 covers render, click, variants, disabled; no arrow-key test; no binding in apps/storybook/a11y/patterns.test.ts.
findings.fix: After k02-choice-5, bind the radio pattern in patterns.test.ts and add an arrow-key selection test.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: Slider has no bound APG pattern, can render an unnamed thumb, and loses its rail in forced colors.
findings.evidence: slider.json contract.accessibility null; not in patterns.test.ts; slider.tsx:98-104 (getAriaLabel undefined without aria-label/getThumbAriaLabel); slider.css:33-47 (track/indicator background-color only, no border); slider.css:84-87 (focus ring also on pointer drag).
findings.fix: Bind the APG slider pattern and test it; require or warn on a missing label; add forced-colors rules (track border CanvasText, indicator Highlight); ring only on :focus-visible.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: In dark modes the unfilled rail is nearly invisible, so the end of the range cannot be read.
findings.evidence: ui-react-slider-themes-chromium-linux.png rows modern/dark, aqua/dark, terminal/dark; slider.css:38 (rail = --a63-surface-muted). Provisional (taste); not contrast-measured.
findings.fix: Use a rail token with at least 3:1 against the surface in dark mode (or add a border), and recheck the themes baseline.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: Disabled and dragging states are listed but never captured, and the thumb has no hover state.
findings.evidence: slider.json states [rest, focus-visible, dragging, disabled]; grep 'disabled' slider.stories.tsx: none; slider.css has no :hover rule.
findings.fix: Add a disabled story and a hover style for the thumb; capture both in baselines.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: Slider and Progress default to the accent tone, which contradicts AGENTS.md rule 5; their docs pages are one-line generated stubs.
findings.evidence: CLI: slider tones default accent, progress tones default accent; AGENTS.md rule 5: 'Selection is neutral by default; set tone="accent" on a selection, Slider or Progress only when it is one of those cues.' No slider.mdx or progress.mdx; generated pages from component-catalog.ts:470-476,586-592. The range onValueChange caveat lives only in slider.tsx:30-33. Applies equally to progress.
findings.fix: YZ decides which is right: change both contract defaults to neutral, or reword rule 5. Then add docs pages for slider and progress with usage, the range API and the tone rule.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: Controlled and ranged change handling is untested.
findings.evidence: slider.test.tsx:7-51: no controlled-range test, no onValueCommitted test, no APG test.
findings.fix: Add tests for controlled single and range values, pointer drag commit, and the APG slider pattern.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: The input Rating works only controlled.
findings.evidence: rating.tsx:12 (value required), 77-87 (value forced, no defaultValue); props are cast onto RadioGroup (line 86).
findings.fix: Add defaultValue for the input form (uncontrolled via RadioGroup defaultValue) and type the input-mode props as RadioGroupProps.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: Rating looks the same in all 4 themes and both modes.
findings.evidence: ui-react-rating-themes-chromium-linux.png: 8 identical star rows; rating.css uses only --a63-category-amber and text-secondary for every theme. Provisional.
findings.fix: Decide whether the choice archetype should show per theme (e.g. retro outline weight, terminal glyph), and label the theme rows like the other Themes stories.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: Rating's accessible names are hard-coded English.
findings.evidence: rating.tsx:50 (`${value} out of ${max}`), rating.tsx:90 ('1 star' / `${star} stars`); only the group label is a prop.
findings.fix: Add a getItemLabel(star) prop (and a formatter for the read-only name), defaulting to the current English.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: Rating has no docs page beyond the generated stub, and its contract names no accessibility pattern.
findings.evidence: No rating.mdx; component-catalog.ts:491-497; CLI answer for rating has no 'Accessibility pattern' line; rating.json contract.accessibility null.
findings.fix: Bind the radio pattern for the input form in rating.json, and write a docs page covering read-only versus input use.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: Rating's keyboard, hover, disabled and half-value behaviour is untested.
findings.evidence: rating.test.tsx:9-27: three tests only.
findings.fix: Add tests for arrow keys, disabled input, and the 4.5 read-only fill width.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: Progress tracks are nearly invisible in terminal/dark and retro/dark.
findings.evidence: ui-react-progress-themes-chromium-linux.png rows retro/dark and terminal/dark; progress.css:29-32 (track = --a63-field-background with border-subtle). Provisional; not measured.
findings.fix: Give the track a token with at least 3:1 against the surface (or a stronger border) in those themes.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: Complete has no distinct design, and reduced-motion indeterminate looks like 40%.
findings.evidence: Contract outcome 'Completion is distinguishable' (CLI); progress.css has no data-complete rule; Steps story only shows a full bar at 100 (progress.stories.tsx:50); progress.css:52-55,73-78.
findings.fix: Style [data-complete] (e.g. success tone or check) and a distinct static indeterminate; capture both.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: The indeterminate sweep runs the wrong way in RTL.
findings.evidence: progress.css:64-71 (physical translateX keyframes) while Base UI anchors the bar at insetInlineStart (ProgressIndicator.mjs:29).
findings.fix: Flip the keyframes under :dir(rtl), or animate inset-inline-start instead of translateX.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: AtomProgressView announces a hard-coded English 'In progress'.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-ios/Sources/Atom63UI/AtomProgressView.swift:69-72 (return "In progress" as String, not LocalizedStringKey/String(localized:)); no distinct complete treatment.
findings.fix: Use String(localized:) with a bundle-resolved key, and add a complete state to match the contract.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner exports no props type, has no size axis, and injects a <style> per instance.
findings.evidence: spinner.tsx:5-25,27,39; CLI 'Types: None'; spinner.json has no axes; no spinner.css, so check:craft never sees its CSS.
findings.fix: Move the CSS to spinner.css, export SpinnerProps, add a sizes axis (sm/md/lg on the control icon sizes) to spinner.json.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner's role=status has no text, so loading is usually not announced.
findings.evidence: spinner.tsx:30-34 (role=status + aria-label on an empty svg); the Playground pairs it with visible text that is outside the live region (spinner.stories.tsx:14-19).
findings.fix: Default the svg to aria-hidden and let the caller own the status text, or render visually hidden text inside a status wrapper; document which.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner has no themes matrix and no archetype.
findings.evidence: Baselines: only spinner playground, sizes, dark; spinner.json visualArchetypes []. Provisional.
findings.fix: Add a Themes story; YZ decides whether the spinner should vary per theme.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: The reduced-motion state is listed but never captured.
findings.evidence: spinner.json states [loading, reduced-motion]; spinner.stories.tsx:13-34 has no reduced-motion story.
findings.fix: Add a reduced-motion story (prefers-reduced-motion emulation) with a baseline.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner sizes are set with inline pixels, off the token scale.
findings.evidence: spinner.tsx:15-16 (fixed 1rem); spinner.stories.tsx:25-27 (style 12/20/32px).
findings.fix: Covered by the sizes axis in k02-choice-28; switch the story to it.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner has only the generated docs stub and an almost empty CLI answer.
findings.evidence: No spinner.mdx; component-catalog.ts:593-598; CLI shows no axes, archetype or types.
findings.fix: Write a docs page (when to use Spinner versus Progress or Skeleton, labelling) after k02-choice-28/29.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner tests check only render and className.
findings.evidence: spinner.test.tsx:7-17.
findings.fix: Add tests for the accessible contract chosen in k02-choice-29 and for the reduced-motion rule.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: No subject in this batch is covered by check:control-alignment, so their 44px targets are unguarded.
findings.evidence: scripts/design-system/check-control-alignment.mjs:40-61,92-104 lists only Button, Toggle and Input markup; sweep control-alignment.log 'passed (3 rungs × 8 axis combinations)'.
findings.fix: Add checkbox, radio, switch, slider thumb, rating input and segmented items to the coarse-pointer target assertions.

findings.subject: batch
findings.summary: All 8 components are marked stable but none meets the readiness bar.
findings.evidence: maturity 'stable' in packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/{checkbox,radio,switch,segmented-control,slider,rating,progress,spinner}.json; every subject above has a criterion at 2 or lower.
findings.fix: Either fix the P1/P2 findings or lower maturity until the scorecards are ready (layer-2 reviewer to reconcile).

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: Neutral tone fills with a text token (baseline token-role debt), and Slider ignores the shared selection accent.
findings.evidence: craft-baseline.json:18-19 (progress.css and slider.css background-color: var(--a63-text-primary)); slider.css:46 and progress.css:37 use --a63-action-primary directly while checkbox/radio/switch use --a63-selection-accent (checkbox.css:11).
findings.fix: Add a fill token for the neutral track tone (e.g. --a63-track-fill-neutral) and route accent through --a63-selection-accent; remove the two baseline entries.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: No forced-colors rule; the checked fill is lost even though the check survives.
findings.evidence: checkbox.css:86-89 (fill is background-color); no forced-colors block.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors block (checked border/fill Highlight) together with k02-choice-1.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: Checkbox and radio add a 13px margin around the box on touch, on top of the ::after target, so layout shifts between pointer types.
findings.evidence: checkbox.css:26 and radio.css:32: margin max(0, (min-target - size) / 2) = (44 - 18) / 2 = 13px on coarse; the ::after already provides the target. No phone story for either.
findings.fix: Drop the margin and rely on the ::after target (as Switch and Slider do), or document the reserved space; add a phone story.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: checkbox.mdx says there is no per-theme code and lists tokens that are out of date.
findings.evidence: checkbox.mdx 'Theme sheet' and 'Tokens it reads' omit --a63-choice-box-shadow, -shadow-checked and -indicator-gloss (checkbox.css:14-16).
findings.fix: Update the mdx token list and theme note.

findings.subject: radio
findings.summary: Focus-visible, hover and pressed states are designed but never captured in this batch's baselines.
findings.evidence: All baselines are static rest states (e.g. ui-react-radio-states, ui-react-switch-states, ui-react-rating-input); radio contract lists focus-visible; switch press squash at switch.css:126-128.
findings.fix: Add play-function stories that focus or hover one control per component so baselines capture the ring.

findings.subject: switch
findings.summary: Switch and Rating hover styles are not gated by @media (hover: hover), so they stick after a tap.
findings.evidence: switch.css:122-124; rating.css:83-88 (checkbox.css:94-98 and radio.css:96-100 gate correctly).
findings.fix: Wrap both rules in @media (hover: hover).

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: In terminal/dark the neutral selected plate barely separates from the track.
findings.evidence: ui-react-segmentedcontrol-themes-chromium-linux.png terminal/dark left control (cropped and enlarged); tokens: segment-selected-background terminal = surface-muted, segment-track-background terminal = field-background (atom63 token). Provisional.
findings.fix: Raise the terminal selected background or add a border for the neutral plate.

findings.subject: switch
findings.summary: iOS counterparts are snapshotted only in the default theme, and web axes (switch size, segmented tone/variant/size) have no iOS mapping.
findings.evidence: examples/ios-demo/Atom63DemoTests/__Snapshots__/iPhone-17-Pro_iOS-26.2/{toggle,radioGroup,segmentedControl,slider,progress}.{light,dark,large-type}.png only; AtomToggle.swift takes no size; segmented-control crossRenderer maps Picker(.segmented) only.
findings.fix: Add theme snapshots (aqua/retro/terminal) and state the unmapped axes as platform adaptations in the contracts.
